title: Paranormal investigators describe hauntings at Franklin's Octagon Hall
excerpt: Footsteps with no one there. A teapot that flew off a shelf. Apparitions walking through a dining room. Paranormal investigators and staff at Octagon Hall in Franklin say the hauntings are real — and they're sharing their most unforgettable encounters.
content:
What This Story Is About

  • Paranormal investigator Cameron Hesson and Octagon Hall director of operations Beth Allen describe firsthand encounters with footsteps, voices, moving doors, apparitions and physical incidents — including a hair-pulling encounter and a teapot that moved and struck Allen — at Octagon Hall in Franklin, Kentucky.

What Happens Next

  • Octagon Hall hosts paranormal investigations and other events throughout the year, with additional ghost hunts during the Halloween season.

For Context

  • Octagon Hall has a Civil War history, including use as a field hospital. Those who study the paranormal there say some experiences seem to repeat, while others appear to respond to visitors in real time.

FRANKLIN, Ky. (WBKO) - Some say one of the most haunted buildings in Kentucky is right in our backyard.

At Octagon Hall, some hear footsteps coming from an empty room, see a door moving on its own, or hear a voice without anyone there to speak.

For paranormal investigator Cameron Hesson, those experiences are nothing unusual.

“You hear footsteps throughout the night, voices talking to you that aren’t there, they’re not attached to a physical body. You’ll see doors opening and closing, things moving by themselves,” Hesson said.

An encounter that stood out

Hesson has spent years investigating the hall, but one encounter still stands out. While walking upstairs with a friend, he says he felt something grab and pull his hair. There was just one problem.

“He looked at me, he’s like ‘Brother, I hate to be the one to tell you this, but you don’t have hair,’” Hesson said.

He says he could feel the pull so strongly that he could feel his scalp move.

A teapot incident

He’s not the only one who says something at Octagon Hall has gotten physical.

“One of the other more recent things was actually some activity where a teapot. We could not see it on the cameras because the camera was not on the teapot, but it’s silver. So, it’s got some weight to it. But the knives were laid out where you could see the image. You could see the teapot shaking. It came off, hit a cup, and hit me in the back of the head,” said Beth Allen, director of operations at Octagon Hall.

Apparitions reported inside the home

Allen says she’s seen apparitions inside the home. Just recently, she says a group was sitting in the dining room when a man walked past the doorway.

“We knew we were the only people here in the home, and a man walked by clear as day. We all saw him past the doorway,” Allen said.

Perhaps the most talked-about spirit at Octagon Hall is a little girl named Mary.

“Her dress caught fire because the ambers from the fire hit her dress. And she was severely burned,” Allen said.

Others have reported seeing a woman in white and figures they believe could be former residents of the home.

“They found something that they were attached to and that emotionally they were fully invested in. And although their physical time on Earth was done, they didn’t want to leave,” Hesson said.

A history rooted in the Civil War

The hall also carries a heavy Civil War history, including time used as a field hospital. Those who study the paranormal here say some experiences seem to repeat, while others appear to respond to visitors in real time.

Whatever the explanation, after years of investigations, one thing is certain: there are plenty of stories still walking the property of Octagon Hall.

Octagon Hall hosts paranormal investigations and other events throughout the year, with additional ghost hunts during the Halloween season.
